title: Annotatio I §.IV open SPECIFICA: Testimonies acknowledging impropriety — Fathers explicit; stop before Picherellus catalog
pass_a_gloss: §. IV. The arguments touching the specific nature of the proposition still under inquiry are chiefly made up from the testimonies of those who acknowledge and confess its impropriety in species, either expressly and explicitly, or through their interpretations and so implicitly. EXPLICITLY they establish it as figurative (1) the MORE ANCIENT FATHERS OF THE CHURCH, whose testimonies with greatest industry Oecolampadius among the first Reformers collected in a Dialogue, Melanchthon in an Epistolary counsel sent to Frederick the Palatine; Among more recent writers Johannes Jonstonus the Reformed, Syntagma on the Communion of the ancient Church ch. 3 art. 3 §. 3 from p. to me 86 to p. 100. And Petrus Picherellus the Pontifician, Theological Opuscula p. 28.
pass_b_english: §. IV. Arguments for the specific nature of the proposition under debate are drawn chiefly from those who acknowledge its impropriety in species — expressly, or implicitly by their interpretations.
EXPLICITLY figurative: the more ancient Church Fathers (collected by Oecolampadius and Melanchthon), the Reformed Jonstonus, and the Pontifician Picherellus (Opusc. Theol. p. 28).
Stop before the Picherellus / Tertullian catalog and further SPECIFICA testimonies.
source_text:
§. IV.
Argumenta, specificam propositionis, de qua adhuc disquiritur, naturam attingentia, istorum potissimum testimoniis conficiuntur, qui improprietatem ejus in specie, vel disertè atque explicitè, vel per interpretationes suas, sicque implicite, agnoscunt ac confitentur. EXPLICITE figuratam statuunt (1) PATRES ECCLESIAE ANTIQUIORES, quorum testimonia summâ industriâ collegit ex primis Reformatoribus Oecolampadius, in Dialogo, Melanchton, in consilio Epistolico, ad Fridericum Palatinum misso; Ex recentioribus Johannes Jonstonus Reformatus Syntag. de Commun. veteris Ecclesiae cap. 3. art. 3. §. 3. à pag. mihi 86. ad pag. 100. Et Petrus Picherellus Pontificius Opuscul. Theol. p. 28.
